problem.title: Bookings don't only get lost on the phone.
problem.text: Someone wants a table or a service. They call during service, or message you at eleven at night, and nobody answers. They rarely try twice. They go to the next place on the list. The reservation was there. It just went somewhere else.
problem.point1_desc: The phone goes when every hand is already full.
problem.point2_desc: People decide to book in the evening, long after you have closed.
problem.point3_desc: A chat or a DM sits unread until someone gets to it tomorrow.
problem.solution: Reserve AI answers the calls and the messages, takes the booking, and puts it in your book, in German or English.
problem.lede: A missed call is just the most visible case. An ordinary week in a business that is doing well:
problem.r1_what: Fully booked, nobody free to pick up
problem.r5_what: Second call from the same guest
problem.close_lead: None of these customers get in touch again.

faq.title: Have Questions?
faq.subtitle: Here are answers to the most common questions about Reserve AI.
faq.a1: Usually just 24 to 48 hours. We handle all the technical configuration. You just need about 15 minutes for a quick onboarding call.
faq.q2: Will customers notice they're talking to AI?
faq.a2: Most customers experience the conversation like chatting with a friendly assistant. We tailor the tone specifically to your business so it feels natural.
faq.q3: Does it work with my existing system?
faq.a3: Yes, Reserve AI integrates with over 95% of common booking and POS systems: Booksy, Treatwell, SimplyBook.me, Google Calendar, and many more.
faq.a4: Absolutely. No long-term contracts, no hidden fees. Cancel with 30 days' notice anytime.
faq.q5: What happens if the assistant can't answer a question?
faq.a5: For unusual requests, Reserve AI captures the caller's details and notifies you immediately via SMS or email so you can call back.
faq.a6: German and English by default. We can add more languages like Slavic languages, Arabic, or French on request.
faq.a7: Setup starts at €500 and increases for more advanced workflows or integrations. That covers configuration, training, and launch. After that, you pay your monthly package fee.
faq.a8: Yes! We offer a 14-day money-back guarantee. You can also book a free demo before signing up.
faq.q9: How secure is my customer data?
faq.a9: Fully GDPR compliant. All data stored on secure European servers with 256-bit SSL encryption. We never share your data with third parties.
faq.a10: We specialize in German service businesses. Fast setup, German support, local data storage, fair pricing, and personal service.
faq.contact_text: We're here to help! Book a free demo or contact us directly.

svc_booking.title: The POS built for AI-handled bookings.
svc_booking.subtitle: Reserve POS is the operating layer behind Reserve AI. It stores the business rules, checks real availability, manages bookings and orders, and gives staff a clean place to review what the assistant did.
svc_booking.visual_alt: Reserve POS dashboard with booking, order, and reporting controls
svc_booking.hero_stat1_label: Safe API boundary for the voice assistant
svc_booking.hero_stat2_label: Staff review for drafts and handoffs
svc_booking.model_title: Reserve AI talks. Reserve POS checks. Staff stay in control.
svc_booking.model_subtitle: Most POS tools only record what staff type in. Reserve POS is designed so the AI assistant can safely read business data, create drafts, and hand work to the team.
svc_booking.model1_text: Reserve AI answers the call, understands the request, and collects the details needed for a booking, order, or handoff.
svc_booking.model2_text: Reserve POS checks hours, catalog, customer records, availability, table or service rules, and tenant permissions before anything is confirmed.
svc_booking.model3_text: Bookings, orders, call events, and uncertain requests land in staff workflows with review, edit, confirm, or reject actions.
svc_booking.capabilities_title: One system for bookings, orders, customers, and AI actions.
svc_booking.capabilities_subtitle: Reserve POS connects the work that happens after a call: what was requested, what was checked, what was created, and what staff need to do next.
svc_booking.cap1_text: Review AI-created bookings, handoffs, and pending actions before they affect the operation.
svc_booking.cap2_text: Check service slots, staff, rooms, tables, capacity, opening hours, and conflict rules before offering a time.
svc_booking.cap3_text: Keep caller details, phone numbers, notes, visit history, language preference, and booking history in one tenant-scoped record.
svc_booking.cap4_text: Track sales, payments, daily activity, AI-attributed bookings, missed-call recovery, and operational performance.
svc_booking.cap5_text: Support product catalogs, open tickets, table selection, Bons for bar or kitchen, and payment close flows.
svc_booking.cap6_text: The voice agent uses authenticated POS endpoints for reads and writes instead of touching the database directly.
svc_booking.difference_title: Different from a normal POS because it was designed around the AI workflow.
svc_booking.difference_subtitle: A generic POS can record a sale. Reserve POS also knows what the assistant said, what it checked, what it drafted, and what staff still need to approve.
svc_booking.generic1: Staff manually enter bookings after a call or copy details from another tool.
svc_booking.reserve1: The assistant can draft the booking through POS APIs, with customer details, source, notes, and audit trail attached.
svc_booking.generic2: Availability is often separate from calls, tables, services, staff, and business rules.
svc_booking.reserve2: Availability is checked against the real operating data before the AI offers a time or confirms next steps.
svc_booking.generic3: AI activity is invisible, so managers cannot see what was automated or why it needs review.
svc_booking.reserve3: AI actions, handoffs, call events, and pending confirmations appear in staff review workflows.
svc_booking.generic4: Reports show sales, but not which bookings or revenue were influenced by missed-call recovery.
svc_booking.reserve4: Reports can connect calls, AI actions, bookings, orders, and revenue so the owner sees the value of automation.
svc_booking.flow_subtitle: Reserve POS gives the assistant a safe way to act, and gives staff a clear way to approve or complete the work.
svc_booking.flow1_text: Reserve AI answers and identifies the request: booking, order, question, change, or handoff.
svc_booking.flow2_text: The assistant reads business profile, catalog, customers, and availability through POS endpoints.
svc_booking.flow3_text: Reserve POS creates a draft booking, order, handoff, or call event with tenant-safe validation.
svc_booking.flow4_text: The team sees what happened, confirms safe work, edits edge cases, or rejects anything uncertain.
svc_booking.flow5_text: Owners see booking outcomes, order activity, AI-attributed work, and missed-call recovery over time.
svc_booking.cta_title: Show customers the assistant. Show staff the control layer.
svc_booking.cta_subtitle: We can walk through how Reserve POS would map your services, tables, customers, booking rules, AI Inbox, and reporting before you connect the assistant to real operations.

team.title: Built by people who know the rush.
team.subtitle: We are four best friends in Berlin who have all worked in gastronomy. We know what a busy service feels like when the phone ringing while guests are waiting, orders moving quickly, and a team trying to keep everything together.
team.story: Those experiences are why we started Reserve. We are building the tools we wished we had ourselves without taking the human side out of hospitality.
team.goal: We are starting with one clear goal to run Reserve as a restaurant’s real phone line and real till for a full month, learn from the people using it every day, and prove that it works when service gets busy. Then we improve it and move on to the next restaurant.
team.contact_line: Questions before then? Email us and one of us answers.

founder_story.title: It started at a hackathon
founder_story.lede: We formed the team on day one and picked the most ordinary problem in the room. By the end of that week, the thing we had built picked up a phone and took a booking.
founder_story.s1_title: Day one, a team and a problem
founder_story.s1_p1: Summer Up Hackatron, summer 2025, through CODE University in Berlin. We formed the team on the first day and went looking for something to build. We did not have to look far. All four of us had worked in gastronomy, so the problem chose itself.
founder_story.s1_p2: Restaurants and cafés miss calls and messages. Someone wants to reserve, ask a question, or order, and the phone rings while the staff are already running. The booking does not wait. It goes somewhere else, and nobody in the building ever finds out.
founder_story.s2_title: What we set out to build
founder_story.s2_p1: An assistant that takes the call like a person. Handles calls and messages, books the table straight into the calendar, and remembers what the guest actually wanted: the window seat, two cappuccinos, oat milk.
founder_story.s2_p2: Not a form on a website. Not another inbox for someone to check. The phone rings, something answers, and the booking is in the book.
founder_story.s3_p1: We built it that week with n8n, Twilio and GPT, on far too much coffee, losing a good part of one night arguing with Ngrok tunnels at three in the morning.
founder_story.s3_p2: Then it worked. The AI picked up a call, answered like a person, and logged the reservation. That was the moment it stopped being a demo. We had all heard that phone ring a hundred times in real jobs and watched nobody get to it. This time something did.
founder_story.s4_title: From one week to the real thing
founder_story.s4_p1: The hackathon ended. The problem did not. So we rebuilt it properly: the phone agent, the chat agent, and the till the booking lands in, as one system instead of three that pretend to know about each other.
founder_story.s4_p2: We are early, and we would rather say so. No long customer list, no numbers to impress you with. One goal: one restaurant, running Reserve as their real phone line and their real till, for a full month. Not a pilot everyone is polite about. The real thing, on a real Friday night.
founder_story.s4_p3: We learn from the people using it every day, fix what breaks, and prove it holds. Then we do the next one. If that sounds like your place, we would like to talk to you.
founder_story.cta_title: Want to be the first one?
founder_story.cta_text: Tell us about your business and we will show you what Reserve would do on your busiest evening.
